thesis: Marvell reports fiscal Q2 after the close today (Aug 27), an unresolved binary event with consensus at roughly $2.71B revenue (+35% YoY) and $0.93 non-GAAP EPS, and options pricing a ~11-12% two-sided move. The disclosed items in hand are the Aug 18-19 Alphabet warrant (58.97M shares, ~7% of shares outstanding, strike $206.58 below the $245.12 close) tied to a custom-chip agreement worth up to ~$120B cumulative if all milestones hit, and a confirmed 4% pullback into the print. The stock trades at roughly 58x forward earnings against Broadcom's ~20x on similar AI exposure, insiders have been net sellers over the trailing year including a CEO sale days before the Google news, and Broadcom retains its own multi-year TPU deal with Google through 2031 -- so the 'Marvell displacing Broadcom' framing is contested rather than settled. A mid-July -8% single-session drop on sector-wide AI-capex sentiment, unrelated to Marvell's own results, shows the stock is highly exposed to macro repricing independent of its fundamentals. This suggests no basis for establishing a position hours before the event that will reprice it.
invalidation: The Aug 27 print and guidance clear expectations and the shares hold their post-print level, at which point the setup can be re-screened with the binary resolved.

thesis: SpaceX's Q2 capex ($18.37B, of which $15.83B AI-infrastructure) has not moderated; on Aug 25 the company announced a further $100B Starbase spaceport in Louisiana, stacking a new decade-plus capital commitment on top of the existing buildout. The Colossus 2 gas-turbine litigation (NAACP v. xAI/MZX Tech) remains unresolved -- the Aug 24 preliminary-injunction hearing was postponed with no new date confirmed, and the compliance deadline to remove the unpermitted turbines runs to July 2027, outside the near-term window. A new $570M contractor lien dispute (Darana Hybrid, countersued by SpaceXAI) surfaced in early August, pointing to payment friction on the same data-center buildout that supports the $45B Anthropic contract. Q2 revenue did beat (+92% YoY) and Starlink connectivity remains the only profitable segment, but at 51 real daily bars since the June IPO there is no 200-day trend to judge the drawdown against. This suggests the capital-intensity and litigation questions remain open rather than resolved by the beat.
invalidation: Capital expenditure guidance moderates while connectivity margins hold, the Colossus 2 turbine litigation resolves (or a rescheduled hearing clears it) without disrupting the Anthropic contract, or the Darana Hybrid contractor dispute settles without a further liquidity strain.

thesis: Intel's Q2 2026 revenue rose 25.4% YoY to $16.1B and the Q3 guide of $16.3B came in roughly 8% above consensus, both already-disclosed results. Against that, the $23B equity offering priced at $95/share (closed mid-August) leaves the stock still about 7% below what allocators paid at $88.26, the fourth dilutive capital event in about a year after the Nvidia, SoftBank and U.S. government stakes. Competitive erosion is also disclosed and ongoing: combined x86 share fell to 69.3% (a 30-year low) as AMD hit a record 30.7%, and a published Qualcomm Snapdragon benchmark beat the closest comparable Intel client chip by roughly 53%, sending the stock down 7% on Aug 18. Separately, the U.S. Supreme Court has scheduled oral argument for October 2026 in Anderson v. Intel, an ERISA case over the company's 401(k) plan menu -- a confirmed near-term hearing, though not a fraud or solvency matter. This suggests the data-center growth trajectory is real but still funding itself through dilution while competitive share keeps eroding, even though the same offering also finances the capacity producing that growth.
invalidation: Q3 revenue misses the $16.3B guide, the shares fail to reclaim the $95 offering price, x86 share losses continue to accelerate, or a further equity raise is announced.
sources: Intel Newsroom ($20B offering upsized and priced): https://newsroom.intel.com/corporate/intel-announces-upsize-and-pricing-of-20-billion-common-stock-offering
Law360 (SCOTUS Oct 2026 argument in Anderson v. Intel): https://www.law360.com/washington/articles/2509623

thesis: AMD's Q2 (reported early August, quarter ended Jun 27) beat on both lines -- $1.66 EPS vs $1.62, $11.55B revenue vs $11.28B -- with data-center revenue more than doubling (+107% YoY), and Q3 guidance of about $13B came in above the ~$12.52B consensus. The strongest counter-evidence is Elon Musk's Aug 4-5 statement that SpaceX will build its new 'Starmind' orbital compute program exclusively on Nvidia's Blackwell platform, reversing an earlier dual-sourcing expectation -- a concrete, company-specific negative, not just sector sentiment. It doesn't change the read here: SpaceX was not yet a large current AMD revenue contributor, AMD separately added Microsoft as a Helios rack-scale customer in mid-July, and the disclosed data-center growth and raised guide both post-date and outweigh the single-customer setback. The $4.75B raised Aug 14 was senior unsecured notes (debt, not equity), so it adds leverage without diluting holders, and no OpenAI/Meta warrant-vesting milestone has been triggered. Shares at $481.01 sit 17.7% below the 52-week high of $584.73. This suggests the disclosed fundamentals have genuinely strengthened even with one real customer-specific setback.
invalidation: Data-center revenue growth decelerates on the next print, another major named customer moves volume to a rival, or an OpenAI/Meta warrant-vesting milestone is triggered in a way that materially resets reported EPS expectations.

thesis: Abercrombie's Q2 (reported Aug 26) showed record net sales of $1.27B (+5%, 15th consecutive quarter of growth) and diluted EPS of $4.17 against $1.99 consensus, with full-year EPS guidance raised to $13.10-$13.60. Stripping the roughly $100M pre-tax IEEPA tariff refund booked as a cost-of-sales reduction (a one-time item stemming from the Supreme Court's February 2026 ruling striking down IEEPA tariffs), adjusted EPS was still about $2.42, a real beat, but comparable sales were flat company-wide with Hollister comps down about 3%, so the reported growth is coming from store/regional expansion (APAC +19%) rather than same-store demand. Shares already rose roughly 35-37% on the print. Separately, former CEO Mike Jeffries' sex-trafficking trial is now confirmed proceeding -- a judge ruled him mentally competent to stand trial on Aug 21, with jury selection scheduled for Oct 26, 2026, about 60 days out. This suggests entering after a one-day repricing of this size, on a beat that is partly mechanical with flat underlying comps and a headline-risk trial in two months, carries poor reward for the risk.
invalidation: A subsequent quarter shows comparable sales turning positive without further tariff-refund benefit, or the shares retrace materially toward the pre-print level while headline litigation risk fades without an adverse outcome.
sources: The Motley Fool (15th consecutive quarter, tariff detail): https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/26/abercrombie-fitch-just-delivered-its-15th-consecutive-quarter-of-sales-growth-heres-the-real-reason-the-stock-is-skyrocketing/

thesis: Biohaven's SK Biopharmaceuticals licensing deal for opakalim (Kv7 platform), disclosed Aug 26, carries a $795M headline value, but only $400M is upfront cash and even that is split -- $350M contingent on HSR antitrust clearance and other closing conditions not yet met, $50M deferred a year -- with $150M more milestone-contingent and $245M representing assumed liabilities rather than incoming cash. RBC Capital called the deal 'a fairly surprising' monetization of Biohaven's most mature, most valuable asset, reading it as a liquidity-driven trade of commercial upside for near-term cash rather than a value-accretive partnership from strength. As of Jun 30, cash and marketable securities of about $267.8M roughly matched the six-month net loss of $267.8M even before this deal, and the company had already expanded its ATM program and filed a new omnibus shelf in the same period -- both signaling continued reliance on external capital rather than the licensing deal closing the funding gap on its own. This suggests the deal improves optionality without resolving the underlying liquidity question.
invalidation: The $350M closing payment is confirmed received and cash runway is disclosed extending materially past 2027 without a further equity or debt raise.

thesis: Kanzhun's Q2 (reported Aug 25) showed revenue of RMB2.40B, +14.1% YoY, and operating income up 32.6% YoY to RMB863.2M with adjusted operating margin at 43.8% (+1.9pp) -- genuine operating leverage. The headline net income figure (+173% YoY) is misleading on its own: roughly RMB1.5B of it came from a one-time non-operating fair-value gain on an investee's IPO, and adjusted net income excluding that gain and stock comp grew only 9% YoY, slower than revenue. Q3 guidance of RMB2.41-2.50B (11.4-15.6% growth) brackets rather than clearly extends the 14.1% run-rate, so the acceleration case is not proven, and analyst price targets are unusually dispersed ($15-28). A previously-flagged Robbins LLP 'investigation' traces to a fully-settled 2021 class action (final court approval Feb 2023), not a new 2026 matter -- no current litigation with a scheduled next step was found. This suggests a profitable, buyback-funded platform with real operating leverage continuing to compound at a steady rather than accelerating pace.
invalidation: Q3 revenue lands below the RMB2.41B low end, operating margin gives back the year-over-year gain, or the buyback pace slows materially.

Robbins LLP page (dated to the closed 2021 matter, not a new 2026 investigation): https://robbinsllp.com/kanzhun-limited-aug-21/
SEC EDGAR Form 424B3 (2021 class action settlement notice): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1842827/000110465922127912/tm2227102-6_424b3.htm

thesis: Semtech's fiscal Q2 (reported Aug 25) beat on both lines -- revenue $341.9M, +32.7% YoY and about 4% above consensus, adjusted EPS $0.71 vs ~$0.61 -- with Q3 guidance at a $410M midpoint roughly 14% above the pre-print consensus, and infrastructure/data-center revenue up 69% YoY. The strongest counter-evidence is that the pending CopperEdge securities class action (alleging this same management overstated demand and ramp timing across a Nov 2024-Feb 2025 class period) was granted class certification on May 20, 2026 -- a real escalation from merely 'pending,' and it goes directly to whether this management's guidance can be trusted. It doesn't change the read here: class certification is a procedural finding about commonality across plaintiffs, not a merits ruling on the underlying allegations, no hearing or trial date is currently scheduled in the case, and a related shareholder derivative suit over the same facts was dismissed on demand-futility grounds in August 2026. Semtech is also divesting its cellular module business to Compal for $62M (announced Aug 13, closing not expected until Q4 2027), a portfolio move unrelated to the litigation. This suggests the disclosed operating trajectory has genuinely inflected even with an unresolved securities case in the background.
invalidation: Q3 revenue lands below the $405M low end of guidance, a court sets a near-term hearing or ruling date in the CopperEdge class action, or new demand-overstatement evidence surfaces.
sources: Kessler Topaz (CopperEdge class action, certification status): https://www.ktmc.com/semtech-corporation/
